ideas.title: AI-written tests that pass but catch nothing: proof that a suite would catch a regression
ideas.edge: witness, the estate's mutation gate, already does this and is live

evidence.said: CI bloated with untargeted AI test slop that has not been mutation tested or checked by a human.
Mutation testing found a test passing even when the method returned an empty string; AI tests at scale will have this problem.
The open problem is verifying that agents' tests actually test what they are supposed to.
When one AI writes the code and its tests, the tests confirm its misunderstandings and passing suites hide broken apps.

ideas.title: A hard spend cap for AI agents that actually holds, with a receipt of what was spent
ideas.edge: kar-tally (an MIT verifier skill) and the spend wall the estate runs on its own API key

evidence.said: Charged $1,771 in four hours against a $25 spending limit.
A monthly spending limit was not enforced, allowing overage charges.
Asks for a per-session spend cap in interactive sessions; the budget flag works only in print mode.
A runaway agent left running for twenty minutes ran up a surprise bill, so the author built a kill switch.

ideas.title: A tamper-evident audit record of every tool call an agent makes, that a regulator can verify
ideas.edge: the trust rail (receipts re-run by anyone) and fallcore-mcp in front of the FallCore proxy's log

evidence.said: An outline for a tool-call audit record a regulator can verify.
A proposed standard: a tamper-evident audit record contract for MCP.
Add immutable logs and approval gates for any agent action touching money, data exports or production.
Enterprises need MCP providers to tell whether a call came from a human or an LLM, and audit it.
Most teams deploy agents with no behavioural monitoring, credentials leaking into logs, and zero audit trail.

ideas.note: The rescan the same day found the complaining evidence it lacked. The test offers only what exists: every agent call to your own model goes through one logged proxy (fallcore-mcp in front of FallCore). That is not yet the regulator-verifiable, tamper-evident record people ask for, and no post may say it is.

ideas.title: A check that every legal citation in an AI-drafted filing exists, before it reaches a court

evidence.said: US court decisions involving lawyers' AI hallucinations: 207 in 2025, 361 so far in 2026 (third-party count).
Law firms are wary of AI tools after hallucinated citations led to sanctions, fines and a licence suspension.

ideas.why: Two dated items only; the October sanctions coverage found was from October 2025, older than a year. A daydream until a third recent source (ideally someone paying for a check) is found. A same-day rescan (Hacker News) found no third recent source.
